scope_limit: Complete within the reviewed questionnaire boundaries, not the entire campaign or national census.

coverage.title: Maryland House of Delegates District 39, 2026 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Five candidates' full published answers to five common questions, republished from Vote411 by Maryland Matters. The publisher explicitly distinguishes these unedited candidate answers from its edited campaign biographies. Exact pre-primary release/version is unverified, so all answers are downloadable but not enrolled in the dated model corpus. Amar Mukunda is absent from this guide; absence is not a verified nonresponse, withdrawal or no-platform finding.

coverage.title: Wisconsin governor, 2026 Democratic primary: housing
coverage.coverage_note: All six tracked Democrats' complete published housing-response blocks from PBS Wisconsin's April22 episode. Named speaker headings delimit answers; reporter narration, the Republican response and Missy Hughes, who is outside this tracked ballot field, are excluded. The transcript preserves edited published responses, not an unedited interview. Source dates do not imply that Barnes or Rodriguez remained active at the August primary.

coverage.title: Wisconsin governor, 2026 Democratic primary: data centers
coverage.coverage_note: All six tracked Democrats' named response blocks from the February18 PBS episode. Reporter claims in the common introductory prompt are retained as the prompt, not adopted as independently verified facts or included in candidate model text. Hong's response here is not silently expanded into a full moratorium pledge. Candidates may have made additional or later proposals elsewhere.

coverage.title: Wisconsin governor, 2026 Democratic primary: school funding and vouchers
coverage.coverage_note: The January30 PBS transcript has two separate named-speaker rounds. Every tracked Democrat's complete published block is preserved for each round. Headings and exact answer ranges prevent another candidate or reporter entering the response. A call for scrutiny is not automatically an abolition pledge, and a candidate's description of current voucher law is not independently certified legal guidance.

coverage.title: Wisconsin governor, 2026 Democratic primary: first governing priorities
coverage.coverage_note: All six tracked candidates' answers to PBS's first-bill prompt, published January16. The interview dates precede later withdrawals. These explicitly stated priorities support campaign-framing comparisons, not measured message frequency or proof that unmentioned policies were opposed. The publisher's Francesa Hong name typo is explicitly reviewed and retained in the source heading.

coverage.title: Wisconsin governor, 2026 Democratic primary: cross-party governing
coverage.coverage_note: Six complete named responses from the January21 PBS episode. Claimed legislative accomplishments remain attributed self-descriptions. The publisher's Joe Brennan heading is explicitly associated with the canonical Joel Brennan record through the same original interview series. These answers do not justify assuming the DSA-endorsed candidate rejects all bipartisan work.

coverage.title: Hawaii Congressional District 1, 2018 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Complete answers to Civil Beat's twelve questions for six candidates, not all campaign material or the complete primary field. Ed Case's separately reviewed interviews are not substitutes for questionnaire answers.

coverage.title: Illinois Congressional District 7, 2020 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: All four primary candidates answered WTTW's three questions. Exact publication and pre-primary version remain unverified, so these full answers are available for qualified comparison but are not enrolled as timing-supported classification inputs. Separately submitted opening campaign statements support the reviewed claims but are not additional questionnaire answers.

coverage.title: Illinois Congressional District 8, 2022 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both Democratic candidates answered all four WTTW questions. The retained 2022 primary guide has no verified original publication/version date, so answers remain timing-qualified and are not enrolled as dated model inputs. Candidate allegations and quoted third-party schedules are preserved as speech, not independently verified findings.

coverage.title: Travis County District Attorney, 2024 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates supplied responses to all three Community Impact questions before the primary. The publisher requested answers under fifty words; complete responses to this format are not complete campaign platforms. Performance claims and personal self-descriptions are attributed, not independently audited.

coverage.title: Pittsburgh City Council District 7, 2023 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates answered WESA's five questions. Candidate answers are separated from reporter biographies and source captions. Numerical claims about housing output, buyers and budgets remain attributed statements rather than independently verified statistics.

coverage.title: Allegheny County Council District 11, 2023 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates answered all five WESA questions. Complete responses retain shared opposition to privatizing Shuman, support for more council resources, and differing policy emphases without treating an unmentioned proposal as opposed.

coverage.title: Wisconsin Assembly District 76, 2026 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: All five candidates answered City Cast Madison's seven questions before the primary. The original named-answer format is preserved. The restaurant question is nonpolicy context and does not enter policy-model inputs. Near-duplicate public-bank answers attributed to Bennett and Sullivan are preserved but withheld from model inputs and independent policy comparison pending attribution review.

coverage.title: Massachusetts House, 26th Middlesex District, 2016 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates supplied all five answers to The Somerville Times before the September 8 primary. Biographical introductions, publisher text, and comments are excluded from the answer-only corpus. The marijuana question is a real policy disagreement; both oppose the current charter-cap ballot question despite disputing past records.

coverage.title: Allegheny County Controller, 2023 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates answered WESA's five questions before the primary. Accusations, self-described records and financial assessments remain attributed statements, not independent audit findings. The candidate answers are separated from reporter biographies and captions.

coverage.title: Minnesota Senate District 65, 2022 DFL primary: campaign priorities
coverage.coverage_note: Both responding Senate candidates' complete answers to the shared priority question are retained. coverage.title: Fairfax County Braddock District, 2019 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates' complete responses to GGWash's six housing and transportation questions are retained. Stated fiscal amounts, population statistics and claimed effects are candidate assertions, not independent audit findings.

coverage.coverage_note: Both candidates' four submitted Surveyor responses are retained in full. coverage.title: Mississippi US Senate, 2018 Democratic primary
coverage.coverage_note: Five candidates' complete five-question submissions are retained. Omeria Scott's questionnaire was not recovered; this is not a no-position label.
